I ran `proposals.apply` with `record.py apply` on a scratch copy of HEAD's record. All 9 entries were rewritten and `record.py check` gave 0 failures. Nothing was applied to the real record and nothing was committed. Meaning is unchanged in all nine. Together they go from 3,908 to 7,870 characters, and seven are well over 600. The growth is the words given to pointers and the definitions.

- **P-79:** "So the demos that fail today are respelled" read as already done, and "climb batch 20's rung I" was a batch handle. Now "is to be respelled" (the work is owed). The example names the change by what it did (P-153, the integer power). Each ledger row (670, 710, 791, 731) gets its own words, so a reader can see which path each demo fails on.
- **P-80:** "sign-refined" named no type, and "return with covariance" could read as final or as deferred. Now the types are defined from the question he answered, with `NN32` and `NN64` set apart, and the return is stated as P-62 states it. The handle "the S1 form" became words.
- **P-84:** "Storage is `double[]`" could be read as covering every array, and "built together" read as an order of work. The title is narrowed to `RR64` arrays, which is the question he answered. "Together" now means what he rejected: sizes held only as run-time fields first, sized types later. I added "Built" and "Still to build" lines, sourced from F-67 and P-85.
- **P-85:** the fork-3 default seemed to contradict "no default", and "the whole preparation ... is done" read as a fact. Now fork 3 is stated as an agent's later default that is not his answer. The preparation line now reads as a rule, and way 4a is described by what it does. The audit's two questions on this entry still stand.
- **P-87:** "the model", "the vocabulary" and decision D were undefined. All three are now defined, with the refused `planeSum` repair as the example. The diff-rule sentence keeps its wording, because the audit's question on whether that rule is his still stands.
- **P-88:** "as the type system promises (row 299)" and "under `Array2`" were opaque. Row 299 is now given by the cost it records. `ReadableArray2` is described by the library's `ReadableArray1` pattern. The trait is kept as wanted, per his page comment of 10-21 at 23:29 UTC.
- **P-89:** a cold reader asked whether a function-taking `fill` remains. Now both methods are stated with their arguments, the rename is explicit, and the reason comes after "Why:".
- **P-90:** "Gating row 331 on static-argument inference" was a ledger row plus a handle. The parked proposal is now stated in words and row 331 moved to the note. The `where`-clause gate keeps its wording, since the entry is held for his answer.
- **P-91:** "bare" could read as "without type arguments", and the marker was unnamed. Now there are examples (`Box`, `Box[\ZZ32\]`, with no marker and no hash code, from the entry's first text) and the marker is named. Both still-to-build items get their row's and PLAN's words, including the "declares or inherits" condition of row 321.

One new question for the curator, on P-88: does `ReadableArray2` fix the shape of the read-only matrix? The immutable-arrays probe of 10-20 proposes a standalone `ImmutableArray2` instead.

- P-79: blocked. It never says whether "kept running" means walk, the compiled path or both. The list of failing demos can be read as the ones with a known repair or as all of today's failures. It is unclear when to rewrite a demo and when to wait for the feature. "self-type rule" and "get no instance" under P-48 are not in the skill. The five demos and the "timing line" are not named.
- P-80: mostly clear. "Their return is P-62's" can be read two ways (who decides whether they come back, or that they will come back). The `covariant` keyword and covariant static parameters are not in the skill, which says generics are invariant. It is unclear what "Built" covers.
- P-84: mostly clear. It is unclear whether size checking is built or only the `nat` parameters. "a first store" can be read two ways. It conflicts with P-85: here `double[]` is decided, while P-85 keeps the array questions open with "no default" and says decision A "puts" `double[]` in place.
- P-85: blocked. It does not say whether the three questions are the same items as decisions A, B and D or separate ones. "Preparation" versus "the work" is not defined, so a worker cannot tell what may be done now. It does not say whether way 4a is in the tree and can be relied on. "read as fixed for the call" is a checker idea the skill does not explain.
- P-87: mostly clear. "Nothing of it" may mean decision D or any change to a model line. It does not say whether D is approved (P-85 still lists it as open). It does not say whether phase 5 comes after the switch-over.
- P-88: mostly clear. "13 to 54 times as high" as what is not said. It is unclear whether `ReadableArray2` is decided or only wanted, who files its ledger row, and how it relates to `Diag`. The first two parts have no built or to-build status.
- P-89: clear.
- P-90: mostly clear. "Not tried before then" has no clear "then". The claim that neither path implements a `where` clause in an `extends` clause seems to conflict with the skill's `compiler.md`.
- P-91: blocked on one point. The entry says the debug marker, such as the Java class name, goes in `asDebugString`, but also that `asDebugString` should print walk's `a Box: Box`, which is not the Java class name. The "where it reaches every object" clause can attach to the PLAN item or to the overflow itself.
